comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi @participant3 

You are not by any chance running into this? #15901
If yes, you find the solution here in my last comment on that issue: https://github.com/Lightning-AI/lightning/issues/15901#issuecomment-1505754665

If no, try also this:
- Use `strategy="ddp"` instead of "ddp_spawn"
- Upgrade Lightning to a more recent version

Without any code or any error trace, there is not much else I can do to help. Please consider providing this information, and also the version numbers of your packages, otherwise we won't be able to help or work on this. Thank you for your understanding.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi @participant1, my PyTorch_lightning version is "1.5.1", PyTorch version = "1.10.0", 
This is my trainer config file - 
_target_: pytorch_lightning.Trainer

gpus: 0,1 # Specify GPU by CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 
min_epochs: 1
max_epochs: 800
log_every_n_steps: 5
precision : 16
num_sanity_val_steps : 0 # This does not work with dp, only with ddp
check_val_every_n_epoch : 1
benchmark: True
overfit_batches: False
accelerator: ddp

I am initialising the DDPPlugin with this code,
if cfg.trainer.get('accelerator',None) == 'ddp': # for better performance in ddp mode
        print("HI")
        # plugs = DDPPlugin(find_unused_parameters=False)
        plugs = DDPSpawnPlugin(find_unused_parameters=False)
    else: 
        plugs = None
        
I'm initialising my trainer using this code 
trainer: Trainer = hydra.utils.instantiate(
            cfg.trainer, logger=logger, _convert_="partial", plugins=plugs ,callbacks=callbacks,
        )
        
Where can I use the strategy keyword. Also, what versions of both PyTorch and PyTorch_lightning should I update too?
Thanks

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Yes sorry, this is quite an old version of Lightning and "strategy" as an argument doesn't exist there, it is still under the `plugin` argument. So use `plugs = DDPPlugin(find_unused_parameters=False)` in this case.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: HI @participant1, I used this case only, and it gave me an error saying that some parameters are not taking part in loss calculation and needed to be searched, soo set the "find_unused_parameters" argument to True. I did that, and I faced with another issue. Should I reproduce the issue and send it? Will I face error with new version?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Yes, it is possible you need to set `find_unused_parameters=True` but that's unrelated. What I'm saying is try to use `plugs = DDPPlugin(...)` insteasd of `plugs = DDPSpawnPlugin(...)` and see if that helps.

> Should I reproduce the issue and send it? Will I face error with new version?

It's always best to have a small reproducible example to work with. Otherwise we can guess forever. Also, in your post you never sent any error message or stack trace, which would have been useful as well. 

> Will I face error with new version?

I can't say for sure, because you haven't provided much information for us to check that.

comments.body:
Hey @participant3 I'm sorry but it is difficult for me to help here. I see a couple possibilities:

a) You're using an old version of Lightning (1.6) and in the new version this problem was fixed. Solution: Upgrade Lightning
b) The problem is in any of the Lighntning version. Solution: We need a reproducible code sample to be able to know which conditions lead to this. 
c) The problem is not in Lightning, and instead in the user (your) code. Solution: Based on the error, you need to check a few things. 1) Check that you are not calling backward yourself or calling it twice in a row for some reason. 2) Have you overridden the `backward()` or `optimizer_step()` hooks in the LightningModule? If yes, something might be wrong there. d) Run your script with `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL python train.py ...` as suggested in the error message to see which parameter name shows up.  
e) Replace the model with a dummy model that's very simple, like a single linear layer. If this works -> Issue is with the model. If this doesn't work -> Issue is might be with the training code.
f) If there is gradient checkpointing in your model, you'll probably have to turn it off (as suggested in the error message). 

These are the main points that come to mind. Please understand that it is almost impossible to help you with this little information you have provided, and that the Lightning version you are using is quite old for me to remember any details or known issues from back then.
